notice: Synthetic data only. NASHA is a concept, not an operating business. Every scenario was executed; nothing is hand-written.

scenarios.title: Discrepancy to approved DRAFT purchase order
scenarios.claim: A flagged inventory discrepancy becomes a draft purchase order only after a different, authorised human approves the exact call.

scenarios.title: A role without the procurement tool is blocked by THE WEIR
scenarios.claim: The quality-lead policy does not contain the write tool at all, so no approval is even requested.

scenarios.title: An approval that expires before the human decides is refused
scenarios.claim: Approvals have a 15-minute lifetime enforced by the gateway store; a late approval creates nothing.

detail.detail: approval expired before it was granted

scenarios.title: A proposal changed after approval cannot use that approval
scenarios.claim: The approval is bound to the exact call hash, so a 50% larger quantity needs a new approval.

scenarios.title: An instruction hidden in supplier text is treated as data
scenarios.claim: The note is labelled untrusted, flagged, excluded from claims, and the proposal is unchanged.

scenarios.title: Replays and duplicates create nothing new
scenarios.claim: A used approval is single-use and a repeated request with the same idempotency key returns the original run.

scenarios.title: Malformed model output fails safe
scenarios.claim: Schema validation with two bounded retries, then abstention; no proposal and no approval request. The model here is a scripted test double, not a real language model.

scenarios.title: Tenant B's identity cannot act in tenant A
scenarios.claim: Each tenant has its own signing secret, warehouse, ledger, approval store and memory; a token from another tenant fails signature verification.

nodes.name: Synthetic orders
nodes.note: Deterministic simulator; per-tenant seeds and sizes.

nodes.name: Warehouse pipeline
nodes.note: Source contracts, incremental month partitions, quality gates and a publish gate (SQLite).

nodes.name: PostgreSQL variant
nodes.note: Same models transpiled to PostgreSQL and reconciled table by table; rounding-tie regression tests.

nodes.name: Recipes, BOM, inventory, variance
nodes.note: Depletion from synthetic orders x BOM; variance detection scored against injected anomalies.

nodes.name: Ingredient demand forecast
nodes.note: Seasonal baselines and Holt-Winters with rolling-origin backtest.

nodes.name: Ops AI tool layer
nodes.note: Fixed-SQL read tools, role and site gate, audit rows; no language model.

nodes.name: Governed agent (planner + validation gate)
nodes.note: Rule planner; structured-output model planner exercised only with scripted test doubles.

nodes.name: Incident investigation
nodes.note: Reconstructs who, tenant, tools, evidence, policy decision, block reason and side effects from one correlation id.

nodes.name: Evaluation + mutation testing
nodes.note: Independent oracles; deliberately broken variants must be caught.

nodes.name: Release gate
nodes.note: PASS / FAIL / REQUIRES_REVIEW from machine-readable evidence; missing evidence never passes. Not yet run on remote CI.

nodes.name: THE WEIR gateway
nodes.note: The real mcp_weir Gateway (separate repository, pinned) enforces per-role default-deny policy and holds writes for single-use, call-bound, expiring approvals.

nodes.name: Human approval
nodes.note: Tenant-scoped identity, role check, maker-checker, approval bound to the exact call.

nodes.name: Procurement ledger (draft POs)
nodes.note: Schema cannot represent a sent order; idempotent writes; hash-chained audit.

nodes.name: Run traces and correlation ids
nodes.note: One correlation id per run; every tool call, decision and failure class is recorded.

nodes.name: Multi-tenant isolation
nodes.note: Separate stores and signing secrets per tenant; shared code, process and reference recipe files are NOT isolated.

nodes.name: Retrieval (BM25, hybrid, pgvector)
nodes.note: pgvector HNSW test runs on an embedded PostgreSQL.

nodes.name: Language-model runtime
nodes.note: No local model runtime in this environment; the real-model smoke test is skipped and unverified.

nodes.name: Production AI Agent Platform
nodes.note: Ideas and adapted code (hashing embeddings, RRF) are reused in NASHA; the platform package is not imported and no runtime integration exists.

nodes.name: Website demo
nodes.note: The portfolio replays recorded evidence; it calls no live backend.
